_what: Paradise Pool outline, traced from georeferenced aerial imagery.
_why_this_file_exists: Karen asked for a blue shape the shape of the pool where the pool should be.
The pool had only a landmark pin before, which put the label in roughly the
right place but drew nothing -- so the biggest amenity in the Town Center was
invisible on a map whose whole job is showing what is there.
_how_measured: Thresholded, not drawn by hand. Treated pool water is the one surface down
there with a colour of its own: it samples b-r > 25 at value > 120 and
saturation > 0.25, where the stormwater ponds are the same blue but far darker
(value 39 measured) and every roof and path is bright but neutral.
Google prints its own place marker on top of the pool, which punched a notch
out of the water, so the mask is closed over the icon and its enclosed holes
filled before the outline is traced with marching squares.
The mask is then opened once with a 3 m disc, because an outline good to
+/-3 m must not claim detail finer than that -- and because closing over the
marker can bridge a stray blue speck to the pool and leave a spur. That is a
rule applied to the whole mask, not a vertex deleted by hand; it cost 28 m2.
Georeference is the same 1.0348 m/px solve the Town Center buildings and courts
use, fitted from the court rectangles at rms 1.5 m, so the pool cannot drift
Verified the way everything here is verified: drawn back onto the imagery.
_accuracy: About +/-3 m, and 1,245 m2 of water. It is a traced outline of a real edge, not a survey, and it is drawn with a soft edge to say so.
_not_included: A second bright-blue blob of 318 m2 sits about 80 m north-west, by the Latitude
Bar and Chill. It was dropped: at this resolution a small blue roof and a small
pool are the same thing, and an extra blue shape beside the water would read as
name: Paradise Pool
